name: HyperbrowserScrape
title: Hyperbrowser Scrape
description: Scrape a single URL to markdown, HTML and links with a stealth headless browser
whenToUse: Pick to grab the content of ONE known URL as markdown, HTML and links. It reads a single known page; following links across a site, pulling typed fields against a schema, and finding URLs by query are all different jobs with their own nodes.

package.name: hyperbrowser
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# FULLY DECLARATIVE. Three nodes, one vendor, one key.
#
# SPLIT OUT OF `crawl`, which held these three alongside two Apify nodes. That package was
# one only in the sense that both vendors do "web scraping"; they share no endpoint, no
# credential and no shape. ApifyResults is a stateful iterator driven by a `continue`
# back-edge, which is computation and stays TypeScript, so keeping one package would have
# meant a package half in each world. Two vendors, two packages.
#
# This is the first package to use `poll`. Hyperbrowser jobs are asynchronous: POST to
# start, then GET the job until it says completed. That loop is why these nodes could not
# be manifests before, and it is now an executor capability every long-running node
# inherits rather than a client this package owns.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/crawl/`.

name: hyperbrowser
displayName: Hyperbrowser
description: Scrape, crawl and extract from the web with a stealth headless browser
version: 1.0.0
category: ingest
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751883548/gravity/icons/HyperBrowser.svg

features:
  - Scrape one page to markdown, HTML and links
  - Crawl a site from a seed URL across many pages
  - Extract typed JSON from pages by prompt or schema
  - Stealth fingerprinting, CAPTCHA solving and country-located sessions

allowedHosts:
  - api.hyperbrowser.ai

requires:
  credential: [apiKeyHeader]
  transport: [json]
  # Every node here waits on a job, and Extract also fans out one request per url. Both are
  # new capabilities, so this package will not deploy to an executor that predates them —
  # which is the point: without `poll` a node settles on the job RECEIPT and emits it as
  # the answer, with nothing anywhere reporting a problem.
  poll: true
  chunk: true
  executorVersion: ">=1.1.0"

credentials.hyperbrowserCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# One key powers scraping, crawling and extraction. Transcribed from the retired
# crawl/src/credentials/index.ts, NAME UNCHANGED so credentials already stored against
# `hyperbrowserCredential` keep resolving after the node moved packages.

name: hyperbrowserCredential
displayName: Hyperbrowser
description: Hyperbrowser API credentials for scraping, crawling and extraction
documentationUrl: https://docs.hyperbrowser.ai

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Hyperbrowser API key from app.hyperbrowser.ai
    placeholder: ""

shared.hyperbrowser.yaml:
# What every node in this package shares: how to reach the vendor, and how a job finishes.
#
# The retired package had a `startAndPollJob` client for exactly this. It is gone: the
# waiting is `poll` in the executor now, and what is left here is the DESCRIPTION of when
# Hyperbrowser considers a job done, which is the same for all three endpoints.

# The vendor, minus the endpoint. A node $refs this and adds its own url, body and poll.
call: &call
  credential:
    scheme: apiKeyHeader
    header: x-api-key
    value: "{{ credentials.hyperbrowserCredential.apiKey }}"
  headers:
    Accept: application/json
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

# HOW A JOB ENDS, shared by every endpoint here.
#
# `until` is tested against the START reply before any polling, and that is not a nicety:
# the unified /web/fetch endpoint may finish INLINE and hand back the completed result on
# the POST with no jobId at all. The retired client special-cased that too. Without it the
# fast path would be the one that breaks.
#
# `failed` matters as much as `until`. A job that fails terminally and is only tested for
# success gets polled until the attempt bound runs out and then reported as a timeout,
# which sends whoever reads it looking for a slow job rather than a broken one.
finish: &finish
  until: "return response.status === 'completed'"
  failed: "return response.status === 'failed'"
  message: "return response.error || 'no reason given'"
  intervalMs: 2000
  maxAttempts: 90

# THE URL LIST, normalised. Used by Extract in three places (what to fan out over, how to
# label the results, and what to report), so it lives here rather than being written three
# times and drifting.
#
# A template field can arrive as a real array, as a JSON-encoded array, or as one bare URL,
# because upstream nodes and hand-typed config both feed it.
#
# ONE DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE from the retired normalizeUrls: a string that opens with `[`
# and fails to parse THROWS here, where the retired code caught it and treated the whole
# broken string as a single URL. The sandbox has no try/catch, and the old behaviour was
# not better anyway: it turned an authoring mistake into a scrape of a URL nobody meant.
urls: &urls >-
  return Array.isArray(config.urls)
    ? config.urls.map(u => String(u)).filter(Boolean)
    : typeof config.urls === 'string' && config.urls.trim().startsWith('[')
      ? JSON.parse(config.urls.trim()).map(u => String(u)).filter(Boolean)
      : typeof config.urls === 'string' && config.urls.trim()
        ? [config.urls.trim()]
        : []

# ── the session controls, as the two APIs want them ────────────────────────────────
#
# Two shapes, because the vendor has two. The legacy job endpoints (crawl) take a flat
# `sessionOptions` bag of booleans; the modern /web/fetch takes a `stealth` enum and a
# nested `browser` object and SILENTLY IGNORES the old bag. The retired package had a
# function per shape (buildSessionOptions / buildFetchOptions) for the same reason.
#
# Silently is the operative word: sending the wrong shape does not error, it just gives
# you a session with none of the protections you asked for.

# /web/fetch — Scrape and Extract.
fetchStealth: &fetchStealth >-
  return config.useUltraStealth ? 'ultra' : config.useStealth === false ? 'none' : 'auto'

fetchBrowser: &fetchBrowser >-
  return Object.assign({},
    config.solveCaptchas ? { solveCaptchas: true } : {},
    config.country ? { location: { country: config.country } } : {})

# /crawl — the legacy bag. Defaults transcribed from the retired buildSessionOptions:
# stealth and the two page-hygiene toggles ON, proxy and captcha solving OFF, and
# proxyCountry sent ONLY when the proxy is actually in use.
sessionOptions: &sessionOptions >-
  return Object.assign({
    useStealth: config.useStealth !== false,
    useUltraStealth: config.useUltraStealth === true,
    useProxy: config.useProxy === true,
    solveCaptchas: config.solveCaptchas === true,
    adblock: config.adblock !== false,
    acceptCookies: config.acceptCookies !== false
  }, (config.useProxy === true && config.proxyCountry) ? { proxyCountry: config.proxyCountry } : {})

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
#
# Every row defaults its own field rather than trusting the vendor to send it. A page with
# no HTML representation is a real outcome, and `undefined` on a connector reads downstream
# as a broken node instead of an empty one.

- emit: markdown
  from: response
  value: "return (response.data || {}).markdown || ''"

- emit: html
  from: response
  value: "return (response.data || {}).html || ''"

- emit: links
  from: response
  value: "return Array.isArray((response.data || {}).links) ? response.data.links : []"

- emit: metadata
  from: response
  value: "return (response.data || {}).metadata || {}"
files.api/run.yaml:
# ONE CALL, which is also a JOB.
#
# POST starts the fetch and MAY finish inline; when it does not, `poll` follows the jobId
# until it does. The reply this call settles on is the final status payload either way, so
# the events table below reads one shape and never has to know which path it took.

- $ref: hyperbrowser#call
  name: fetch
  method: POST
  url: https://api.hyperbrowser.ai/api/web/fetch

  body:
    url: "{{ config.url }}"
    stealth: { $ref: hyperbrowser#fetchStealth }
    browser: { $ref: hyperbrowser#fetchBrowser }
    outputs:
      formats: [markdown, html, links]
      # "Main content only" maps to Fetch's sanitizer, which strips nav/footer/boilerplate.
      # Off means return the whole page.
      sanitize: "return config.onlyMainContent === false ? 'none' : 'basic'"
    # Only sent when asked for: an empty navigation block is not the same as no block.
    navigation: "return config.waitFor ? { waitFor: config.waitFor } : undefined"

  poll:
    $ref: hyperbrowser#finish
    # The status URL is the start URL plus the job id, and it resolves against the START
    # reply, which is the only place that id exists.
    url: "return 'https://api.hyperbrowser.ai/api/web/fetch/' + response.jobId"
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [url]
  properties:
    url:
      type: string
      title: URL
      description: The URL to scrape
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    onlyMainContent:
      type: boolean
      title: Main Content Only
      description: Strip navigation, footers and boilerplate, keeping the article body
      default: true
      "ui:widget": toggle
    waitFor:
      type: number
      title: Wait For (ms)
      description: Extra time to wait after load for JS-rendered content
      minimum: 0
      maximum: 30000
    # ── session controls, as /web/fetch takes them ────────────────────────────────
    # Deliberately NOT the same set the Crawl node offers. Fetch has no adblock,
    # acceptCookies or proxy toggle, and offering them here would put switches on the
    # panel that the endpoint ignores without complaint.
    useStealth:
      type: boolean
      title: Stealth Mode
      description: Apply anti-bot fingerprinting to look like a real browser
      default: true
      "ui:widget": toggle
    useUltraStealth:
      type: boolean
      title: Ultra Stealth
      description: Maximum anti-detection profile. Slower, so use it only when stealth is blocked
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    solveCaptchas:
      type: boolean
      title: Solve CAPTCHAs
      description: Automatically solve CAPTCHAs encountered during the session
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    country:
      type: string
      title: Location Country
      description: ISO country code to load the page from, e.g. US, GB, FR
      placeholder: US

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`, and the two answer different questions.
    # The manifest is the node author's FLOOR: "this node is inherently privileged". These
    # are the builder's, per box on the canvas, because the same node type legitimately
    # faces staff on one workflow and customers on another.
    #
    # A role especially has to live here: `finance:approve` is a claim THIS deployment's
    # identity provider mints, and a node published to the marketplace cannot know the role
    # vocabulary of every universe that installs it.
    #
    # The executor takes the STRICTER of the two. Neither can loosen the other.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order":
  [authRequired, authRole, url, onlyMainContent, waitFor, useStealth, useUltraStealth, solveCaptchas, country]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: string
    description: URL to scrape
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: markdown
    type: string
    description: Page content as markdown
  - name: html
    type: string
    description: Page content as HTML
  - name: links
    type: array
    description: Links found on the page
  - name: metadata
    type: object
    description: Page metadata (title, description, and whatever else the page declared)

credentials:
  - name: hyperbrowserCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Hyperbrowser API
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

# One page, fetched as a job. A single call that happens to take a while, which is what
# `poll` is for: the manifest says when it is done, the executor does the waiting.

type: HyperbrowserScrape
kind: PromiseNode

name: Hyperbrowser Scrape
category: Web Scraping
color: "#FF6B6B"

description: Scrape a single URL to markdown, HTML and links with a stealth headless browser

whenToUse: >-
  Pick to grab the content of ONE known URL as markdown, HTML and links. It reads a single
  known page; following links across a site, pulling typed fields against a schema, and
  finding URLs by query are all different jobs with their own nodes.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # Idempotent read: the same URL yields the same page, so a prior output may be reused
  # instead of paying for the browser session again (EXECUTION_EFFICIENCY.md §3.2).
  cacheable: true
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

testData:
  config:
    url: https://example.com
    onlyMainContent: true
    useStealth: true
  inputs:
    signal: https://example.com
  expect:
    # A non-empty string, not just a string: an empty markdown would pass a type check and
    # is exactly what a job that "completed" with nothing in it returns.
    markdown: "return typeof output.markdown === 'string' && output.markdown.length > 0"
    links: "return Array.isArray(output.links)"
    metadata: "return typeof output.metadata === 'object' && output.metadata !== null"
